title: Measuring chiral phonons
authors: Rahul Rao, Hanyu Zhu, Nicholas Kotov, Thuc T. Mai, Maria F. Muñoz, Dali Sun, Jun Liu, Wonjin Choi, Renee R. Frontiera, Angela R. H. Hight Walker
abstract: Chiral phonons are quantized vibrations where the atomic motion in a solid breaks improper rotation symmetries. In many cases, chiral phonons possess angular momenta and are therefore selective to circularly polarized light. Both fundamental and applied research efforts on chiral phonons have been gaining increasing attention owing to their importance in a variety of fields including spintronics, spin-selective chemical reactions, thermal transport, quantum information processing and biosensing, where the bi-directional spin-lattice coupling enabled by chiral phonons can be harnessed in new ways, and potentially lead to new functionalities. Thus far, the studies of chiral phonons across diverse materials platforms have evolved largely independently within these fields, but the experimental techniques are often interrelated. In this perspective, we present a detailed description, as well as advantages and disadvantages of the current approaches for experimentally measuring chiral phonons in chiral and achiral materials. We conclude with a discussion of new methods for measuring chiral phonons. Ultimately, this work seeks to offer an experimental guide for systematically investigating the properties of chiral phonons in various materials systems and applications.
summary: This review provides an essential experimental guide for measuring chiral phonons, which are vibrations sensitive to circular polarization. It details advanced spectroscopic techniques like VCD, ROA, and circularly polarized Raman scattering. The work is crucial for harnessing the unique spin-lattice coupling enabled by these phonons in emerging fields like spintronics and quantum information.
main_problem: The paper addresses the challenge of experimentally measuring chiral phonons, which are quantized vibrations whose atomic motion breaks improper rotation symmetries.
main_result: It provides a comprehensive experimental guide detailing various techniques to systematically investigate the properties of chiral phonons across diverse material systems.
method: The review synthesizes multiple experimental techniques, including Optical Rotatory Dispersion (ORD), Circular Dichroism (CD), Vibrational Optical Activity (VOA) (VCD/ROA), and circularly polarized Raman spectroscopy.
model_or_system: The study covers chiral and achiral materials, ranging from crystalline solids like $\alpha$-quartz to 2D perovskites and quantum magnets. Chirality can be inherent or induced transiently via interactions with photons or magnons.
key_observables: Optical rotation, differential absorption (CD), VOA spectra (VCD/ROA), and phonon frequency splitting induced by pseudoangular momentum (PAM).
important_parameters: The magnitude of spectroscopic signatures varies greatly across techniques; the coupling between spin and lattice degrees of freedom is key.
main_assumptions: The primary limitation discussed is the very small signal magnitude associated with VOA measurements, requiring high sensitivity.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate examples of left- and right-handed chiral materials hosting chiral phonons and schematically show the measurement setup for circularly polarized Raman spectroscopy, including phonon dispersion splitting.
paper_structure: The paper is structured as a detailed perspective review, first covering general concepts and then systematically detailing steady-state probe techniques, followed by transient time-resolved spectroscopies.
why_interesting: The focus on spin-lattice coupling and the ability to probe chirality using optical methods makes it highly relevant for understanding quantum phenomena in condensed matter systems, bridging optics and lattice dynamics.
